header.title: REST API documentation
header.subtitle: Complete reference for the {appName} API. Integrate your tools and automate your planning.

intro.p1: The {appName} API is a REST API that lets you read and manipulate your planning data programmatically. All responses are in JSON format (except exports, which return files).
intro.p2: The base URL for all requests is {baseUrl} (the paths below start with /api). Every request must include a valid Authorization header.

auth.p1: The API uses API key authentication. Every request must include the HTTP Authorization header with the Bearer prefix.
auth.p2: API keys use the format hp_ followed by 64 hexadecimal characters. They are created in Settings > API access (“settings:edit” permission, API access enabled) and are shown only once.
auth.p3: A key acts with all the permissions of the user who created it. If API access is disabled, every key-authenticated request returns 503 “{message}”; an unknown or deleted key returns 401.
auth.securityText: Never share your API key. Do not include it in client-side source code. Store it in environment variables. If it is compromised, delete the key immediately (it becomes invalid) and create a new one.

rateLimiting.text: Calls authenticated with an API key are limited to 120 requests per minute per key and 300 requests per minute per IP address. Beyond that, the API responds with 429 Too Many Requests: wait until the next minute before retrying. No X-RateLimit-* headers are returned. Space out automated calls and prefer date filters on large lists.

errorHandling.intro: The API uses standard HTTP status codes. When an error occurs, the response body contains a JSON object with an error field describing the problem.
errorHandling.codeIntro: The error text is written in the language of the request (see Response language). To identify an error in an integration, use the code field instead: a stable identifier (for example errors.notFound) that is the same in every language.

fields.error: Human-readable message, written in the language of the request
fields.code: Stable error identifier (message key, for example errors.forbidden or errors.rateLimited). It does not depend on the language.
fields.params: Optional. Values inserted into the message (for example a limit or a date)
fields.fields: Optional. Per-field errors for the request body: each affected field is mapped to its translated message
fields.details: Optional. Technical details, for example the list of validation errors (422)

statuses.conflict: Duplicate, locked task or daily task limit reached
statuses.unprocessable: Request body rejected by validation (see details)
statuses.tooManyRequests: Rate limit exceeded (per key or per IP address)
statuses.unavailable: API access disabled in the settings

language.intro: Error messages (error, fields) and exported files (PDF, Excel, CSV, iCal) are written in French, English, Spanish or German. Data entered by users (project names, statuses, places…) is not translated, and the code field is the same in every language.
language.order: The language of each request is determined in this order:

steps.cookie: the HP_LOCALE cookie (fr, en, es or de), set by the language selector of the interface;
steps.instance: the instance “Default language” setting (APP_LOCALE, Settings > General > Application), when it enforces a language instead of “Automatic”;
steps.acceptLanguage: the Accept-Language request header (first supported language, according to the q weights);

language.apiKeyTip: Calls made with an API key usually do not send cookies: add the Accept-Language header to choose the language of the messages (unless the instance enforces a language).
language.icalTip: Token-based iCal calendar subscriptions follow the language of the token owner (the last language they used in the interface).

pagination.p1: Only GET /api/tasks is paginated (other lists return a JSON array directly). It accepts the page and limit parameters.
pagination.p2: The response includes the pagination metadata in the root object:

fields.data: Array of results for the current page
fields.total: Total number of results matching the filters
fields.limit: Maximum number of results per page

tasks.list: Retrieves the list of tasks, with optional filters and pagination.
tasks.get: Retrieves the full details of a task, including the assigned users and files.
tasks.update: Updates an existing task. Only the fields sent are changed (partial update).
tasks.delete: Permanently deletes a task and its attached files. Returns the deleted task.

projects.list: Retrieves the list of projects. Archived projects are excluded by default.
projects.get: Retrieves the details of a project, with its owner and group.
projects.delete: Permanently deletes a project AND all its tasks (cascade deletion). Returns the deleted project.

users.list: Retrieves the list of users, with their team and role.
users.get: Retrieves the full details of a user (profile, team, role, qualifications).

teams.list: Retrieves the list of all teams.
teams.get: Retrieves the details of a team, with the list of its members.

statuses.list: Retrieves all available task statuses (used in tasks and filters).

holidays.list: Retrieves the public holidays within a given date range.

vehicles.list: Retrieves the list of all vehicles.
vehicles.assignments: Retrieves vehicle assignments, with optional filters.

config.get: Retrieves all the application configuration settings (key/value pairs).

export.csv: Exports tasks in CSV format (; separator). Requires the export:use permission. Without dates: from today to today + 30 days.
export.excel: Exports tasks in Excel format (.xlsx). Requires the export:use permission. Same parameters as the CSV export.
export.pdf: Exports tasks in PDF format (Gantt). Requires the export:use permission. Same parameters as the CSV export, plus paperSize and orientation.
export.ical: Exports all the tasks assigned to the authenticated user in iCalendar format (.ics), with no filters.

params.searchTitleNotes: Text search in the title and notes
params.limit: Number of results per page (default: 200, max: 10000)
params.endDateOptional: End date (optional: without an end date, the task lasts one day)
params.files: Metadata of files already uploaded (uploads go through POST /api/tasks/[id]/files, as multipart)
params.deleteScope: Recurring tasks: single (default), all, before or after
params.searchProjectName: Text search in the project name
params.searchUser: Search by last name, first name or email
